text:
mike: Quick note — replay harness numbers are ~18% slower than synthetic for the same request mix. wondering if anyone's seen this pattern recently.

anya: hm, are you using keepalive on the synthetic clients? or are they opening a new conn per request?

mike: synthetic uses a pooled async HTTP client with keepalive enabled. replay harness (the one that replays prod traces) replays sockets in sequence and doesn't re-establish until connection churn. suspect connection reuse mismatch.

devon: this screams client-side socket behavior. two quick things to check: 1) TLS handshake rate (new conns) 2) Nagle + small writes causing extra packets.

mike: i captured a short tcpdump — lots of TLS handshakes during the replay window. here's the replay config snippet we use:

```json
{
  "mode": "replay",
  "parallel_sessions": 200,
  "respect_orig_conn": true,
  "delay_scale": 1.0
}
```

sarah: if "respect_orig_conn" is true and traces include many short-lived sessions, you'll end up creating many TLS conns. synthetic harness tends to compact sessions into fewer long-lived connections.

anya: also confirm client keepalive idle/interval settings. default gRPC keepalive can be aggressive. for example, in go client set:

```
grpc.WithKeepaliveParams(keepalive.ClientParameters{Time: 30 * time.Second, Timeout: 10 * time.Second})
```

mike: good call. replay harness uses the java-based replayer that doesn't set keepalive explicitly. will try patching it.

devon: another axis — HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs gRPC. the server's connection handling and batching heuristics expect long-lived multiplexed streams (HTTP/2). replay forcing many HTTP/1.1 conns will defeat batching and KV cache warmup.

sarah: fwiw we saw a perf regression last week after the kernel-selection flip (auto->preferred-vec). the runtime started favoring a vectorized kernel that improves single-stream latency but performs worse under high concurrency because it blocks on a global buffer. could be related: different kernel -> different throughput sensitivity to connection churn.

mike: interesting — i did notice higher stall% in the perf counters during replay. attached a tiny perf dump: 

```
perf_counters: {
  cpu_busy_ms: 1200,
  gpu_util_pct: 78,
  kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.27,
  kernel_idle_wait_ms: 310
}
```

anya: 27% KV cache miss is high for the trace mix. replaying raw requests without preserving prefix locality can hurt kvcache warmup. are we replaying in strict time order or reordering?

mike: strict wall-clock order. traces are from multiple frontends, so locality is scattered. synthetic harness typically groups similar sessions which helps kvcache.

devon: try two experiments: 1) replay with connection folding (force keepalive/pooled conns) 2) replay but group by user/session to preserve prefix locality. compare the delta.

mike: will run both today. quick question: any recommended wrk/grpc load settings to make apples-to-apples?

anya: use these baseline knobs:
- fixed concurrent connections (not unlimited)
- warmup period 120s for KV cache and allocator steady state
- controlled think-time matching P50 inter-request spacing

and for gRPC: use HTTP/2 multiplexing and avoid creating new channels per request (reuse a channel pool).

sarah: add to that: pin the model/kernel choice so the server runtime doesn't switch kernels mid-run. set env `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=preferred-vec` or explicit kernel id. also disable auto-quant fallback during the test.

mike: noted. also, any tips for isolating Nagle/TLS overhead?

devon: two quick checks:
- toggle TCP_NODELAY on the client sockets to see small-packet latency effect
- enable session resumption (TLS ticket) to avoid full handshakes

mike: i'll flip TCP_NODELAY and TLS tickets. if toggling NODELAY reduces latency but increases server CPU, that's sign small writes were the issue.

infra-bot: deploy completed: runtime/2025-03-04 kernel-selection-rollout -> preferred-vec (canary 10%). Monitor channels: eng-runtime, eng-sre.

anya: good to know — if canary is running we might repro the regression in canary clusters too. mike, when you run experiments, tag the cluster and kernel id.

mike: will do. plan: run three runs (synthetic pooled, replay folded, replay-grouped) with kernel pinned and unpinned. collect: p95 latency, qps, kv-miss, kernel-idle, tls-handshakes. report back in this thread.

sarah: if you get consistent delta, file a perf regression with attach profile + tcpdump and @devon for kernel-side follow-up. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks all — starting runs now, will post results in ~90m.
